provenance.generatedBy: claude-opus-5-5 · Field Kit v2 Prompt A batch
provenance.notes: Pro family batch. Small business managed IT is the recurring goal; walk-in repair is the feeder. Copy never promises data recovery, uptime or breach prevention. Certifications and response times are bracketed placeholders. No hardware, software or vendor brand names.

pageStructurePlus.section: Managed IT plans for small offices
pageStructurePlus.contains: Per-seat monthly pricing, what's included (patching, backup checks, help desk hours, new-hire setup and leaver lockout), what is billed extra, and [response time they commit to]
pageStructurePlus.why: Office managers compare managed IT by per-seat price and what's covered. A clear plan page turns break-fix callers into monthly clients.

pageStructurePlus.section: Walk-in and drop-off computer repair menu
pageStructurePlus.contains: Diagnostic fee, screen and keyboard replacement, virus cleanup, slow-laptop tune-up, data recovery attempts with no promised result, turnaround and pickup hours
pageStructurePlus.why: Walk-in repairs pay the rent and bring in the owners of small businesses. A priced menu stops the 'how much to look at it' call.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Wi-Fi coverage surveys, structured cabling, network closet cleanup, firewall and switch installation, before-and-after rack shots and how a project is quoted
pageStructurePlus.why: Network projects are the biggest one-time tickets, and the buyer wants to see tidy work before letting a technician into the ceiling.

pageStructurePlus.section: Backup and security checkup for small business
pageStructurePlus.contains: A checkup of backups, multi-factor sign-in, password practices, old accounts and phishing awareness, with help filling in cyber insurance questionnaires
pageStructurePlus.why: Cyber insurance renewals ask questions owners can't answer. A checkup page catches that moment and leads to a managed plan.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Dental and medical offices, law and accounting firms, construction offices and retail, with the [compliance frameworks they work within] noted plainly
pageStructurePlus.why: A dental office wants an IT provider who already knows dental offices. Industry pages let each owner see their own kind of business.

pageStructurePlus.contains: What counts as an emergency (server down, suspected ransomware, no internet for the whole office), the after-hours rate, and how to reach a technician at night
pageStructurePlus.why: Businesses find a new IT provider on the worst day. A clear emergency page is often how a managed client relationship starts.

designDirections.name: Bench Ready
designDirections.bestFor: Computer repair shops with walk-in hours and some business clients, who need the repair menu, hours and call button first
designDirections.headlineSample: Computer repair and IT support in {City}, walk-ins welcome
designDirections.whyItFits: A dark ground, cyan accent and mono type feel like a network console. Repair menu, hours and the call button lead.

designDirections.name: Office IT, Handled
designDirections.bestFor: Independent IT providers selling managed plans to professional offices, with an IT checkup booked online
designDirections.headlineSample: Managed IT support for {City} offices that can't afford downtime
designDirections.whyItFits: The family's Private Vault combo, kept on purpose: the best managed IT clients are dental, law and accounting offices who trust a quiet, professional look over a gadget look.

designDirections.name: Managed Desk
designDirections.bestFor: Growing managed service providers with several technicians, network projects and industry pages, selling to multi-site businesses
designDirections.headlineSample: IT support and network projects for {City} businesses
designDirections.whyItFits: Carbon and indigo with a neutral grotesque read like a capability statement. Plans, projects and industries sit as cards a buyer can scan.

openers.line: Your Google listing has great repair reviews but no website, so an office manager looking for managed IT support can't see your plans or who you already support.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there's no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Here's what could sit behind that button for an IT support company: {demo-link}

openers.line: The website on your listing opens a Facebook page. A practice owner choosing an IT provider wants your managed plans and security checkup, not repair-shop posts.
openers.hook: Tap their Website link and confirm it lands on Facebook. Note the latest repair or project they posted.
openers.linkLine: A managed IT page built for office owners: {demo-link}

openers.angle: Dated site for an IT shop
openers.line: Your computer repair site still shows an old copyright year and a dead contact form. For an IT business, an outdated site makes owners wonder about their own systems.
openers.hook: Open the site and look for an old year, a broken form or a security warning in the browser. Note which one you found.
openers.linkLine: The same IT company, current and secure: {demo-link}

openers.line: I opened your IT support site on my phone and the menu covered the phone number. When the office internet is down, the owner is searching on their phone.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on your phone and note what breaks. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your IT support site rebuilt for a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: Nothing online says what your managed IT costs per computer or what's included. Office managers comparing providers shortlist the ones who show a per-seat range.
openers.hook: Check every profile for monthly plan information. If there's none, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: Managed IT plans shown as per-seat ranges: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your reviews mention a business owner whose laptop died before tax season and a technician who got the files back. Small business owners searching for IT support never see that off your listing.
openers.hook: Read their reviews and copy one phrase about a rescue, a fast fix or a business client. Quote it back if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Those IT support reviews beside the services they describe: {demo-link}

openers.line: Cyber insurance renewals now ask small businesses about backups and multi-factor sign-in. An IT checkup page that helps answer those forms is what owners search for that week.
openers.hook: Use this any time; mention it if they've posted about security or backups.
openers.linkLine: A small business IT security checkup page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Offices lose their network at the worst times, often after hours or on a Monday morning. When the IT company's number goes to voicemail, they call whoever answers first.
openers.hook: Call their listed number after hours. Note whether there's an emergency option.
openers.linkLine: An emergency IT help page that works at night: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're hiring a help desk technician. Good techs check whether an IT company looks established and has managed clients before they apply.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring note. Note the role and date.
openers.linkLine: An IT support page with a careers section: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your listing says you do on-site IT support around {City}, but not how far. An office in {Neighborhood} wants to know you'll come before they call.
openers.hook: Find towns mentioned in reviews or posts. Use the one furthest from their shop.
openers.linkLine: IT support pages for each area you cover on-site: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your shop takes walk-in computer repairs, but the hours and repair prices aren't anywhere online. People with a cracked laptop screen pick the shop that shows both.
openers.hook: Only if they have a storefront. Check whether hours and prices are listed.
openers.linkLine: A computer repair menu with walk-in hours: {demo-link}

openers.line: Offices letting an IT technician into their network want to see certifications, insurance and how client data is handled. None of that is visible on your profile yet.
openers.hook: Look for any certification they've published. Never quote one they haven't posted.
openers.linkLine: Credentials, insurance and data handling on one IT page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Sounds like most of your managed IT clients come from other business owners. Even a referred office manager searches the IT company before handing over admin passwords.
openers.hook: Look for review text like 'recommended by our accountant' or 'they handle our whole office'. Quote it back.
openers.linkLine: Where a referred IT client would land: {demo-link}

openers.line: When an operating system version reaches end of support, every small office with old computers needs an upgrade plan. A page explaining your refresh service catches that wave.
openers.hook: Use when an end-of-support date is in the news. Don't name the product in the message.
openers.linkLine: A computer refresh and upgrade page for small offices: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you posted is the kind of tidy network work office owners never get to see. It belongs on an IT projects page, not three scrolls down a feed.
openers.hook: Pick their newest post about a rack cleanup, install or rescue and name it exactly.
openers.linkLine: That network project, front and centre: {demo-link}

sequence.dm1:
Hi {Owner}, that {specific recent job} you posted is clean, careful work.

I looked for IT support and computer repair in {City} and found {Business Name}, but no site with your managed plans, repair prices and a way for an office to book a checkup. I put together a sample site to see how it would look, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Want me to send it over?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner}, following up in case my message got buried under tickets. Here's the sample IT support site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It has managed IT plans with per-seat ranges, a walk-in repair menu, a network projects page, a small business security checkup and an emergency help line page. If it's not for you, just say so.
sequence.call:
"Hi, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}, I build websites for independent IT companies here in {City}. I sent you a message a few days ago, did it come through?"

IF NO:
"No worries. Short version: I built a sample site for {Business Name} with managed IT plans, a repair menu and an IT checkup booking, and marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I email you the link?"

IF YES:
"What did you think?"
 → let them talk, don't fill the silence
"I know you could build a site yourself. The point is the managed plan page and the checkup booking, written for office managers, so break-fix callers become monthly clients. The build runs {Build Range} depending on industry pages, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and updates. For you I'd quote about {Build Price}, which is about one office's managed plan for a couple of months."
"Can I walk you through it for ten minutes this week?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a one-page scope and a deposit invoice. We start once it clears, and you can review every technical claim before launch."

objections.objection: I'm an IT guy. I can build my own website.
objections.handler: "You can, and you've had years to. The hard part isn't the code, it's writing managed IT plans and industry pages office managers understand. That's what I bring."
"The best IT clients do. A referred office manager still checks your site before handing over admin passwords, and a plan page closes that referral."

objections.objection: I don't want to publish managed IT prices.
objections.handler: "A per-seat range and what's included is enough. Office managers skip providers who hide everything, and a range filters out the ones who want it for free."

objections.objection: Walk-in repairs are drying up anyway.
objections.handler: "That's why the site leads with managed IT for small offices and keeps repairs as a menu. The walk-in who owns a business becomes a plan client."

objections.objection: I'm too busy with tickets to deal with this.
objections.handler: "Then it's built for that. I draft every page from one call and your past invoices, and you only check the technical details."
"{Build Range}. For you about {Build Price}, for managed plans, the repair menu, the security checkup and a few industry pages. That's a couple of months of one office's plan."

email.subject: IT support site for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "{Owner}, it's {Your Name}. I build websites for IT companies in {City}, and I made a sample one for {Business Name} with managed plans and a repair menu. I'll email the link. Have a look when the tickets settle. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner}, I'm taking the {Business Name} IT support demo down on Friday to free up the space.

Want me to keep it up? One word is fine either way.
sequence.nurture:
Hi {Owner}, year-end is when offices plan computer refreshes and renew cyber insurance. You came to mind.

The IT support site is still here whenever you want it, same price as before. {demo-link} if you'd like another look.

bullets: Lead with managed IT for small business; price walk-in repair pages low, they're the feeder, not the goal.
Peg the build to a couple of months of one office's managed plan, never to an hourly rate.
Industry pages are separate lines, only for industries where they already support clients.
Never write promised uptime, promised data recovery or 'hack-proof'. Use 'attempt', 'checkup' and 'help'.
Price the security checkup booking as its own line; it is the doorway to managed contracts.
Expect the owner to want technical control; offer them edit access and charge for the care plan as hosting and content, not lock-in.

lineItems.item: Managed IT plan page with per-seat calculator
lineItems.description: Max with tiers by seat count, an inclusions table, add-on lines and a quote request that captures device counts.

lineItems.item: Computer repair menu with drop-off form
lineItems.description: Max with repair-by-device pricing, a drop-off form with device details and repair status texts.
Max with a pre-visit questionnaire on backups, sign-in and accounts, and a cyber insurance form help section.
Max when the page covers that industry's common software, compliance notes and a short client story they approve.
Max with before-and-after rack shots, project types and a site survey request.

lineItems.item: Emergency help line page with after-hours routing
lineItems.description: Max with an emergency checklist, after-hours rate display and a text-to-technician option.

whatElseYouSell.name: Technician and workbench photo session
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A short session of each technician, the repair bench and a tidy network closet. Office owners hand admin passwords to people they can see."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, or after a network project they're proud of.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile posts with small business IT tips
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A weekly post on the IT company's Google profile, a phishing example one week, a backup tip the next, so the listing reads like a managed IT provider, not just a repair counter."
whatElseYouSell.when: Day 30, once the site is live.

whatElseYouSell.name: Review requests when a ticket closes
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "When a computer repair or support ticket closes, the client gets a short text asking how it went. Business owners read those before choosing an IT provider."

whatElseYouSell.name: Quarterly security note to business clients
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A short quarterly email to every business the IT company supports: one current scam to watch for, one backup reminder and a checkup booking link."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, once the client list is in one place.

whatElseYouSell.name: Service van lettering artwork
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Van lettering that says 'managed IT and computer repair' with the site address. It sits outside client offices all day where other owners park."

whatElseYouSell.name: Security talk kit for local business groups
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A short slide deck and handout on scams hitting small offices, for chamber and networking breakfasts, ending with the IT checkup booking page."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, when they mention a group they belong to.

whatElseYouSell.name: Cyber insurance renewal campaign
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A landing page and email to local businesses offering help with cyber insurance questionnaires, timed to renewal season, that books IT checkups."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in autumn for year-end renewals.

whatElseYouSell.name: LinkedIn profile for the owner
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Practice managers check the IT owner on LinkedIn before a meeting. I rewrite the profile to match the managed IT plans and industries on the site."

withoutAI.route: The IT company's own business clients
withoutAI.whoPays: Each client business, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Your managed IT clients' websites run on hosting you already see, and plenty are dated. A word from their IT provider is the warmest introduction I'll get."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: The IT provider knows every client's tech and has their trust, so the referral lands with weight.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The agents who send your IT clients cyber insurance questionnaires need better sites themselves. Your security checkup work gives you a reason to introduce me."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Agents and IT providers meet over every cyber renewal and benefit from each other's clients.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The cabling crew you bring in for office network projects needs a site with a project gallery. You're their best referral source."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Cabling subs win work through IT providers and general contractors and rarely market themselves.

withoutAI.whoPays: The camera and access control installer
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The camera installers who need your network for their systems share your small business clients. One introduction from the IT side opens the door."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Camera and IT work overlap on every install, and the referral runs both ways.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The coworking space whose Wi-Fi and network you support needs a member sign-up site. You're in the building every month."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Operators trust the IT provider who keeps the space online and need sites that sell desks.

withoutAI.route: Accounting practices on the support plan
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The accounting firms you keep secure through tax season usually have weak sites. A recommendation from their IT support provider carries real weight."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Accountants have tax-season urgency and trust the technician who saved their busiest week.

withAI.route: Customer question assistant for client businesses
withAI.pitchLine: "Your managed IT clients can add a small assistant on their own sites that answers hours and service questions, hosted on systems you already support."
withAI.whyItWorks: The IT provider handles the setup trust question, and clients pay monthly for a visible improvement.

withAI.route: Cyber questionnaire prep for insurance agents
withAI.pitchLine: "Insurance agents get help pre-filling cyber applications from a client's IT checkup report, drafted for the agent and client to confirm."
withAI.whyItWorks: Cyber applications stall renewals, and agents will pay to move them faster.

withAI.route: Job walk notes to bid drafts for cabling crews
withAI.pitchLine: "Cabling crews on your network projects talk through a site walk and get a draft bid with drop counts and materials to adjust."
withAI.whyItWorks: Faster bids win more work, and the cabling owner saves evenings on paperwork.

withAI.route: Incident clip notes for camera installers
withAI.pitchLine: "When a client asks the camera installer for footage of an incident on their network recorder, an assistant drafts the request log and clip notes for the technician."
withAI.whyItWorks: Footage requests are unpaid time today; a tidy log makes them billable and quick.

withAI.route: Member help desk assistant for coworking spaces
withAI.pitchLine: "Members ask the coworking desk about Wi-Fi, printers and meeting rooms all day. An assistant answers from the space's own notes and escalates real network faults to you."
withAI.whyItWorks: Operators save staff time, and the IT provider gets clean tickets instead of hallway complaints.

withAI.route: Client onboarding checklist assistant for accountants
withAI.pitchLine: "Accounting firms on your IT support plan can send new clients a guided document checklist that answers questions and flags what's missing."
withAI.whyItWorks: Accountants pay to stop chasing documents, and the IT provider already secures the systems it runs on.

softwareAI.name: Missed-call text-back that separates outages from repairs
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A missed call to the IT support line gets a text: whole office down, or one computer? Outages go to the emergency number, repairs get the drop-off form."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs their number forwarded and the on-call contact.

softwareAI.name: Repair drop-off and status tracker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every computer repair checked in with a ticket number, and the customer gets status texts from diagnosis to ready, so the counter phone stops ringing."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their repair steps and pickup policy.

softwareAI.name: Managed IT quote builder by seat count
softwareAI.pitchLine: "An office manager enters computers, staff and locations and gets a managed IT range and a checkup booking, so the first call starts at the right number."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their per-seat pricing and add-on rules.

softwareAI.name: Review reply drafts for IT support reviews
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each new review gets a reply drafted in the owner's voice that thanks the client without describing their network or systems, ready to approve."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs ten past replies. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Support ticket intake assistant
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Clients describe the problem in plain words and the assistant asks the right follow-ups, which computer, what error, since when, then files a clean IT support ticket."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their ticket categories and common questions. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Managed contract invoicing and renewals
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Managed IT invoices go out on the first with the current seat count, and renewal notices go out a month before each contract ends."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their contract list and the payment account they use.

softwareAI.name: Security checkup report builder
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Walk an office through the backup and security checkup on a tablet and a branded report with findings and next steps is ready before you leave."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their checkup checklist and a past report they liked.

softwareAI.name: Checkup findings in plain language
softwareAI.pitchLine: "From the technician's checkup notes, it drafts a one-page summary an owner understands: what's fine, what's risky, what to fix first. The technician edits before sending."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, after the report builder. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Client device inventory portal
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each managed IT client sees every computer, its age, warranty and who uses it, so refresh planning is a conversation, not a guess."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs their device lists by client.

softwareAI.name: Warranty and subscription renewal reminders
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Client device warranties, domain names and software subscriptions get reminders before they lapse, from their managed IT provider, with a quote included."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs renewal dates from their client records.

softwareAI.name: Help article drafts from closed tickets
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Common fixes from closed IT support tickets become draft help articles for the client portal, so printer and password questions answer themselves."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 7. Needs a few months of ticket notes with client names removed. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Client portal with tickets and invoices
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Managed IT clients log in to open tickets, see status, read help articles and pay invoices, which makes a small IT company feel like a large one."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 8. Needs the ticket intake and invoicing in place.

softwareAI.name: Staff joiner and leaver checklist runner
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When a client office hires or loses someone, the manager fills one form and the technician gets the account, device and access checklist for that network."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their onboarding and offboarding steps per client.

softwareAI.name: After-hours outage triage line
softwareAI.pitchLine: "At night it answers the IT support line, works out whether the whole office is down or one laptop is, and wakes the on-call technician only for real outages."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their emergency rules, client list and on-call rota. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Insurance questionnaire answer drafts from checkup data
softwareAI.pitchLine: "For each managed IT client, it drafts answers to their cyber insurance questionnaire from the latest checkup data, for the client and technician to confirm."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs checkup reports and sample questionnaires. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer; the client signs every answer.

softwareAI.name: Help desk technician applicant screener
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Applicants for an IT support technician role answer your questions about skills, driving and on-call, and you only interview the ones who fit."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Whenever they post a role. Needs their must-haves. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Network documentation drafter
softwareAI.pitchLine: "After a site visit, the technician's notes and scan exports become a draft network document for that client: devices, closet layout, passwords vault reference."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 7. Needs their documentation template. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer; never stores passwords in the draft.

softwareAI.name: Monthly client health email
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each managed IT client gets a monthly note: backups checked, updates applied, tickets closed. It reminds them what the plan does while nothing is broken."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs data from their monitoring and ticket tools.

softwareAI.name: Network project quote-to-install board
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every network and cabling project from site survey to quote to install day on one board, with parts ordered and the cabling sub booked."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs their project stages and suppliers.

softwareAI.name: Recurring revenue and ticket-hours dashboard
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See monthly managed IT revenue against ticket hours per client, so the owner knows which contracts pay and which need repricing."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 9. Needs invoices and ticket time by client.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Managed plan page and seat quoter for independent shops
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "The managed IT plan page and per-seat quote builder I built for one shop work for any independent IT company with its own prices loaded."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Most small IT shops never write a plan page; a ready one sells itself.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: IT owners' peer group member template
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The peer group or trade association
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Peer groups for small IT company owners can offer members a managed services site template with plans, checkups and industry pages."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Peer groups exist to help owners grow recurring revenue, and this is a concrete tool for it.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Reseller locator for a regional IT distributor
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Distributors selling to local IT shops can offer a find-a-local-IT-provider map built from the same network and managed IT pages."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Distributors fund reseller marketing, and a locator sends their resellers work.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Template licence for IT marketing agencies
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Agencies that market IT companies can license the managed IT, checkup and network project pages instead of writing them for each client."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies own the relationship; you sell them the hard-to-write structure.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: IT providers serving dental and medical offices
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A set of IT support pages written for dental and medical practices, compliance notes left as placeholders, for any provider who serves them."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Practices buy from IT providers who speak their language, and the pages are reusable.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The repair store group, per location
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Each computer repair store needs its own hours, menu and walk-in page under one brand. I build it once and add each store."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: One contract becomes several locations on the same template.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Vetted IT provider directory for a cyber insurer
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The cyber insurance carrier or managing agency
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Cyber insurers want policyholders to fix gaps before a claim. A directory of local IT providers who run security checkups gives them somewhere to send people."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Insurers pay for risk reduction, and the IT client is the first provider listed.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A chamber security programme page with talks, a checklist and a list of member IT providers, built by the people who run those checkups."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Chambers want useful member programmes, and security is top of owners' minds.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Shop sites for repair training graduates
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The computer repair training programme, per graduate
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Graduates opening their own computer repair business need a repair menu and walk-in page on day one. Programmes can include it."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Training programmes compete on graduate success, and the template is ready.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The acquiring managed services firm, per acquired shop
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Each small IT shop a larger firm buys needs a transition site that keeps local clients calm. I build the move-over pages on the same template."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Acquirers buy shops steadily and need the same transition work on a deadline every time.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: An independent IT company in a new metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I build for one independent IT support company per metro. {City} is spoken for; the next city's best managed IT shop isn't."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: IT owners guard their local market, which makes exclusivity a selling point.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The IT company with a half-built site
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "IT owners who started their own site between tickets and never finished get a complete managed IT and repair site on a build already live."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: They've already tried to do it themselves; finishing it is an easy decision.

upsellLadder.offer: IT support site build plus care plan, one contract
upsellLadder.trigger: They say yes to the demo.
upsellLadder.line: "The IT support site and the care plan go on one contract, so a new plan price or industry page is a text to me."

upsellLadder.offer: Review requests when a ticket closes
upsellLadder.trigger: The first office books a checkup or repair through the site.
upsellLadder.line: "That office found you through the site. Let's ask every closed computer repair and support ticket for a review."

upsellLadder.trigger: Checkup bookings arrive and the owner writes reports by hand afterwards.
upsellLadder.line: "You're writing checkup reports at night. Build them on a tablet in the office and hand them over before you leave."

upsellLadder.offer: Managed IT quote builder by seat count
upsellLadder.trigger: Sixty days of enquiries asking what managed IT costs.
upsellLadder.line: "Every enquiry asks what managed IT costs. Let them enter their seat count and see a range before the call."

upsellLadder.trigger: They sign a third or fourth managed client and tickets arrive by text.
upsellLadder.line: "Tickets by text don't scale past a few offices. Let the assistant ask the follow-ups and file them cleanly."

upsellLadder.trigger: A client calls at night about something that could have waited.
upsellLadder.line: "That late call was a single printer. Let the line sort real network outages from the rest."

upsellLadder.offer: Client portal with tickets and invoices
upsellLadder.trigger: They pass several managed clients and hire a help desk technician.
upsellLadder.line: "With a technician on board and a growing client list, a portal makes your IT support look as big as it is."

upsellLadder.trigger: Their first contract renewals come up.
upsellLadder.line: "Before you renew managed IT contracts, let's see which clients cost more hours than they pay for."
